request: Create an APB GPIO peripheral with interrupts.
expected_behavior: RTL for module apb_gpio (APB4, ADDR_WIDTH 8, 32-bit data, zero wait states, N pins with N 8 by default and 1 to 32 allowed) with DATA_OUT, DIR, a read-only DATA_IN, rising, falling, high and low detection enables, an interrupt enable mask and a write-1-to-clear INTR_STATUS at 0x00 to 0x20, a level irq, and a self-checking testbench, following the approved interface specification and microarchitecture, gated by lint, simulation, and synthesis (and formal, when a .sby is written) before review.
constraints: Work only from the approved interface specification and microarchitecture.
Correct for every N from 1 to 32: bits N and up read as zero and ignore writes.
Lint-clean under Verilator -Wall with no waivers.
known_failure_modes: A write to INTR_STATUS that clears every bit, or bits written 0, or bits in unstrobed bytes.
An edge detector that fires on the level, so a clear never sticks while the pin is held.
A level detector that fires only once, so a clear sticks while the level holds.
A clear that wipes out a detection landing on the same edge.
A self-written testbench that never holds a pin past a clear or clears one bit of several; the held-out reference testbench judges instead.
A self-written testbench that cannot tell a clear-all, an edge on level, a level as edge or an ignored mask from a correct block; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The reference testbench passes on the seat's RTL
The seat's testbench fails each GPIO mutant
The case's N 8 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant
